triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a rename/refactor of caller inputs and could not: the mapping is not one-to-one (pre-fix `entry_is_line_a` drives both the §122 zeroing branch and the China-301 list-1 slot, and post-fix it becomes `entry_is_section_122_exempt` in one rule and `entry_is_china_301_list123` in another), and `entry_is_line_a`/`entry_is_line_b` survive unchanged elsewhere in the same file (lines 1908/1925/2368/2524), so the §122 branch genuinely changed meaning rather than being renamed. The module itself defines those two flags as `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` (HTS 9903.01.32) and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` (HTS 9903.01.33) — IEEPA reciprocal-tariff exclusions — while the §122 rule's own (unchanged) proof atoms cite the 9903.03.03 subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list and the 9903.82.02/.04 metal-article exclusion; resolving `us/statute/hts/9903.03.03` through the pinned release confirms the exemption is keyed to an enumerated note list ("Articles the product of any country, as provided for in subdivision (aa)(ii) of U.S. note 2 to this subchapter"), not to §301 or reciprocal-annex membership. So the pre-fix condition was a branch grounded on the wrong provision, and the fix re-grounds it — untraceable_branch, not a rename, not new coverage. The PR body's "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" plus the enumerated 18 witness-slice exception cells show the old branch produced wrong cell values, ruling out mechanical/not_a_defect.
